topicName: Unit, Integration, System, and Acceptance Testing
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Comprehensive Guide to Testing Levels in Manual QA"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Manual software testing involves several sequential phases to ensure product quality. Understanding Unit, Integration, System, and Acceptance testing is crucial for any manual QA professional to design effective test strategies."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Unit Testing in Manual Context"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"While unit testing is primarily automated and performed by developers, manual testers often engage in white-box testing or component verification during early builds. This involves validating individual functions, methods, or UI components in isolation before integration."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Objective: Verify the smallest testable parts of an application independently."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Responsibility: Primarily developers, but verified by QA through boundary value analysis of isolated modules."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Integration Testing"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Integration testing focuses on exposing faults in the interaction between integrated units or modules. In manual testing, QA engineers verify that data flows correctly between different microservices, databases, or third-party APIs."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Incremental Integration: Bottom-Up and Top-Down approaches."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Big Bang Integration: All components are tested simultaneously."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"Example Test Case: Verify that when a user updates their profile in the UI (Frontend), the change is successfully reflected in the PostgreSQL database (Backend)."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"3. System Testing"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"System testing evaluates the completely integrated system to verify that it meets specified requirements. Manual testers execute end-to-end test scenarios simulating real-world user journeys across the entire application architecture."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Scope: Functional, Usability, Security, and Performance testing."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Environment: Staging environment that closely mirrors production."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Acceptance Testing"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Acceptance testing is the final phase where the software is evaluated against business requirements and user needs. It determines whether the system is ready for delivery and deployment."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Alpha Testing: Performed by internal QA teams before release."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Beta Testing: Performed by actual end-users in a live environment."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"Acceptance Criteria Example: Given a shopping cart with items, when the user clicks 'Checkout', then the payment gateway loads within 3 seconds and processes valid credit cards."}]
